themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street signs across Far Rockaway are failing at an alarming rate this week—20 damaged sign complaints (540% above the 3.1-per-week baseline) and 12 dangling sign complaints (174% above the 4.4-per-week baseline)—suggesting widespread infrastructure decay that poses pedestrian and traffic safety risks.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 20 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.99)
Street Sign - Dangling: 12 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.08)
Combined sign infrastructure complaints represent unprecedented spike in a single reporting period
reporting_angles: Field inspection: photograph damaged/dangling signs; interview DOT about maintenance backlog
Safety angle: Are these hazards creating traffic confusion or pedestrian risk? Any accidents reported?
Budget angle: Connect to recurring CB budget requests for street capital projects—is deferred maintenance finally breaking down?

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked 1500% last week—4 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66)—indicating a potential contamination or discoloration event affecting resident confidence in tap water in Far Rockaway.
evidence: Water Quality complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
Water System complaints remain elevated in top 10 overall (353 over 90 days), suggesting systemic issues
Community Board repeatedly requests DEP capital projects for sanitary sewer development—suggests long-standing water infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Contact DEP: Was there a contamination event, main break, or water main flushing last week?
Resident angle: Interview affected residents about discoloration, odor, or taste issues; check for health-related complaints
Investigation: Cross-reference with any DEP advisories, boil-water notices, or water quality test results from last week

themes_detail.label: Environmental Damage Post-Storm
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints exploded 900% last week—5 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 9.0)—suggesting recent severe weather or environmental stress event has left the Rockaways' tree canopy in crisis.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 5 last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% increase, z-score: 9.0)
Aligns with spike in Snow or Ice complaints (715 over 90 days) and Street Condition complaints (1016), suggesting weather events
Community Board has standing requests to Parks Dept. for park and tree canopy reconstruction/upgrades—indicates pre-existing vulnerability
reporting_angles: Environmental angle: Were there high winds, ice storms, or saltwater surge last week that damaged vegetation?
Parks Dept. response: How fast is Parks addressing tree removal? Are there disease vectors (pests, fungus) affecting the canopy?
Equity angle: Which neighborhoods in the Rockaways are losing tree cover fastest? Correlation with heat/hot water complaints?

themes_detail.label: Noise Disturbance Wave
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged 185% two weeks ago—36 complaints vs. 12.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.96)—and vehicle noise was up 233% the same period (10 vs. 3.0 average), suggesting a coordinated disturbance source or event.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk: 36 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 12.6 weekly average (185% increase, z-score: 4.96)
Noise - Vehicle: 10 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.0 weekly average (233% increase, z-score: 3.88)
Residential noise complaints remain highest overall category (1171 over 90 days), confirming persistent quality-of-life issue
reporting_angles: Timeline investigation: Was there a specific event 2 weeks ago (concert, construction, gathering, enforcement sweep)?
Resident impact: Interview residents affected by the surge; document whether noise has returned to baseline or persists
NYPD angle: Any noise enforcement operations or complaints about specific venues (bars, clubs, events) during that period?

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped 129% two weeks ago—18 complaints vs. 7.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.1)—indicating either coordinated renovation activity or deteriorating building conditions across the district.
evidence: General Construction/Plumbing: 18 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.9 weekly average (129% increase, z-score: 4.1)
Plumbing complaints rank in top 10 overall (352 over 90 days); Heat/Hot Water rank even higher (907), suggesting systemic building issues
DOB filings show 423 total permits in last 90 days (237 alterations, 155 new buildings), indicating sustained construction activity
reporting_angles: DOB records: Cross-reference spike timing with major permit filings; identify which buildings/blocks triggered complaints
Landlord accountability: Are complaints concentrated in specific landlord portfolios? Any pattern in violations issued?
Development angle: Do spikes correlate with active ULURP projects (Edgemere Commons Phase 2B, 14-10 Beach Channel Drive, Arverne East)?
